questions.question_text: Under WV's Fair Housing Act, the Mrs. Murphy exemption applies to owner-occupied buildings with how many or fewer units?
distractors: Two units
Three units
Six units
questions.explanation: The exemption covers "rooms or units in dwellings containing living quarters occupied or intended to be occupied by no more than four families living independently of each other, if the owner actually maintains and occupies one of such living quarters as his residence" (§16B-18-4(a)(2)). Note the critical West Virginia limit: §16B-18-4(a) makes this exemption available "solely for the purposes of familial status," so it is no defence to a claim based on race, colour, religion, ancestry, sex, blindness, disability or national origin.

questions.question_text: A church owns a small apartment building used exclusively to house members. Is this exempt from the WV Fair Housing Act?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, religious organizations housing members are exempt
distractors: No, all housing must comply with fair housing
Only if the building has fewer than 4 units
Only if the church receives no government funding
questions.explanation: A religious organization, or a nonprofit it controls, may limit the sale, rental or occupancy of dwellings "which it owns or operates for other than a commercial purpose" to persons of the same religion, or give them preference (§16B-18-8(a)). Two qualifiers matter: the housing must be non-commercial, and the exemption is lost "unless membership in such religion is restricted on account of race, color or national origin."

questions.question_text: A private country club restricts cabin rentals to members only. Does this violate WV's Fair Housing Act?
questions.correct_answer: No, private clubs may restrict to members only
distractors: Yes, all rental housing must comply
Only if the club receives tax exemptions
Only if the restriction is based on a protected class
questions.explanation: The same subsection also exempts "a private club not in fact open to the public, which as an incident to its primary purpose or purposes provides lodgings which it owns or operates for other than a commercial purpose," allowing it to limit rental or occupancy to members or prefer them (§16B-18-8(a)). Both qualifiers are essential: the club must not in fact be open to the public, and the lodgings must be non-commercial.

questions.question_text: An owner lives in one unit of a four-unit building and wants to discriminate based on race when renting the other units. Does the Mrs. Murphy exemption protect them?
questions.correct_answer: No, the exemption covers familial status only
distractors: Yes, the exemption fully protects the owner
Yes, unless the owner uses a real estate agent
Yes, so long as the owner places no advertisement
questions.explanation: This is a real divergence from federal law. §16B-18-4(a) introduces both the owner-occupied and the for-sale-by-owner exemptions with the words "Solely for the purposes of familial status," so in West Virginia they give no shelter at all for race — or for colour, religion, ancestry, sex, blindness, disability or national origin. The federal exemptions at 42 U.S.C. §3603(b) are not limited that way. Section 1982 of the Civil Rights Act of 1866 would independently reach race discrimination.

questions.question_text: Which of the following entities is NOT exempt from WV's Fair Housing Act?
distractors: An owner-occupied duplex
A religious organization's non-commercial housing
A private club limiting to members
questions.explanation: Licensees and brokerages are never exempt, and involving one destroys the owner's exemption: §16B-18-4(a)(1)(A) makes the for-sale-by-owner exemption available only if the house is sold or rented "without the use in any manner of the sales or rental facilities or the sales or rental services of any real estate broker, agent or salesman." §16B-18-7 separately bars discrimination in the provision of brokerage services.

questions.question_text: A person believes they experienced housing discrimination in WV. With which agencies can they file a complaint?
questions.correct_answer: WV Human Rights Commission, HUD, or state court
distractors: Only the WV Human Rights Commission directly
Only HUD at the federal government level
Only the WVREC and the state circuit court
questions.explanation: All three routes are available, but the clocks differ: a complaint to the West Virginia Human Rights Commission must be filed within one year of the alleged discriminatory housing practice (§16B-18-11(a)(1)(A)), while a private civil action in circuit court may be brought within two years (§16B-18-14(a)(1)(A)).

questions.question_text: After a fair housing complaint is filed with the WV Human Rights Commission, what happens next?
distractors: The complainant must file a lawsuit first
The respondent is immediately fined
The property is placed under a stop-sale order
questions.explanation: The Commission investigates and attempts conciliation. §16B-18-11 requires it to complete the investigation and determine whether reasonable cause exists within 100 days of the complaint being filed, and to notify the parties in writing if it cannot meet that deadline. A charge issues if reasonable cause is found.

questions.question_text: If an administrative law judge finds a discriminatory housing practice, what relief may be ordered under §16B-18-13?
questions.correct_answer: Actual damages, equitable relief, and a civil penalty
distractors: Only monetary fines paid to the state
Only referral to criminal court for prosecution
Only mediation between the involved parties
questions.explanation: An ALJ who finds a discriminatory housing practice must order appropriate relief, which may include actual damages and injunctive or other equitable relief, and may add a civil penalty: up to $10,000 for a first violation, up to $25,000 with one prior violation within five years, and up to $50,000 with two or more within seven years (§16B-18-13(3)).

questions.question_text: After a fair housing charge is issued, how does §16B-18-13 treat the choice between an administrative hearing and a civil action?
questions.correct_answer: A party may elect a civil action in lieu of a hearing, within 20 days
distractors: Both proceed simultaneously to final judgment
Only the Human Rights Commission may choose the forum
A civil action is available only after the Commission dismisses the charge
questions.explanation: Once a charge issues, a complainant, respondent, or aggrieved person may elect to have the claims decided in a civil action in lieu of an administrative hearing, and must make that election within 20 days after receiving service (§16B-18-13). The choice belongs to the parties, not the Commission, and the two forums do not proceed simultaneously.

questions.question_text: A WV real estate licensee discriminates against a buyer based on familial status. Which entities could potentially take action against the licensee?
questions.correct_answer: WV Human Rights Commission and the WVREC
distractors: Only the WVREC for license discipline
Only the WV Human Rights Commission
Only HUD at the federal level
questions.explanation: Familial status is protected by §16B-18-5, enforced by the Human Rights Commission under §16B-18-9, and §30-40-19(a)(27) independently makes discrimination violating any state or federal anti-discrimination law a ground for WVREC discipline. HUD is a further option, but the question asks which entities could act against the licensee — and both state bodies can.
